summary: Run it as is: the change is exact, rules-clean, and self-attributing (the FA3 kernel and the two gather kernels appear as separate rows in the profile), so one run answers the only real question, which is whether FA3's hdim-64 FP8 prefill kernel is limited by the page-size-1 cp.async gather path or by its own softmax/V-transpose ceiling. No landed item interacts with the FA3 call, so no A/B or control is warranted. Expect the per-shape rows to be the signal; the load-level upside is about 1% even if the mechanism fully works.
justification: A. Mechanism: real in FA3. Paged KV uses the TMA path only when page_size is a multiple of kBlockN; at page size 1 (every scored case) the producer warpgroup walks the page table and issues per-row cp.async copies (two 64-byte head rows per token), the path the decode review measured at 1.33-1.73 TB/s. A [B, S, 2, 64] contiguous cache takes the TMA path with no dependent page-table lookup. Profile data (job 62025c368c3c4e8e): the FA3 kernel is 419.9 us (28.0%) on turn_1 full, 1656.1 us (32.7%) on turn_4 full, 4545.7 us (22.0%) on first_turn ctx=32768 full, 8164.1 us (32.8%) on ctx=65536 full, 907 us (4.9%) on ctx=0 full; sliding FA3 is 25.5 / 62.0 / 309.9 us, so the 'flat' sliding rows are right. Converting those to throughput: 2.49e11 FLOP / 419.9 us = 593 TFLOP/s; 9.96e11 / 1656 us = 601; 2.75e12 / 4546 us = 605; 4.95e12 / 8164 us = 606. The kernel sits at a flat ~600 TFLOP/s (30% of FP8 dense peak, 61% of BF16) whether it launches ~96 CTAs plus splits (turn_1, the FlashAttnFwdCombine row proves dynamic split is on) or 2048 m-tiles (first turn). A per-CTA limiter independent of occupancy is consistent with EITHER (i) a latency-bound paged producer (page-table read then row cp.async, two dependent round trips per KV tile, ~1.3 us observed per 176-row tile against ~0.39 us of MMA at peak) OR (ii) the intrinsic FA3 hdim-64 FP8 ceiling (softmax exp per FLOP is 2x hdim 128's, plus the in-smem V transpose FP8 needs); FA3's own hdim-64 numbers are its weakest column and are not far above 600 TFLOP/s. The weakest link is exactly that: the decode evidence (q_len=1, each KV byte used once, bandwidth-bound) does not transfer to q_len=753-16384 where every KV tile is reused across 128 queries and the load path has ~100x more time per byte to hide behind; if (ii) holds, the TMA swap buys nothing and the run only pays the gather. Shapes/directions vs TASK.md: max_pages = ctx + q_len for spread=fixed (reference.py:259), so the gather sizes (21 MB per request at 80K, 83 MB at turn_4) are as stated; but the byte estimates assume near-peak copy bandwidth, and the change as written (fp8 advanced indexing, k_cache.view(-1,hkv,d)[idx]) is a 1-byte-element index kernel over 2x the bytes (read+write): expect 10-60 us at turn_1/first-turn and plausibly 100-250 us at turn_4, not 35 us, i.e. break-even needs a 3-15% FA3 gain on turn_4 full and 2.5-15% on turn_1 full. Weights: full shapes are ~31-34% of every load (turn_1: 16x1435 vs 46x1079; turn_4: 16x4950 vs 46x3367; first turn: the two ctx>0 full shapes are 22% of 3.39 s), and FA3 is ~28-33% of those shapes, so a 10% FA3 gain is ~3% on the full rows and ~1% per load, right at the +-1.5% interval. The run is informative per shape, marginal on the score.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity (only landed item; patch muse_prefill_layer/hypotheses/done/gain/sglang-pipeline-parity.patch): it made the FA3 call byte-identical to baseline.py (paged, varlen q, scheduler_metadata=None on prefill) and feeds the cache rows the gather reads through store_cache; nothing it did changes the FA3 kernel's own time, so it cannot cause or mask a gain here. The one thing to keep is ordering: the gather must run after store_cache on the same stream (the hypothesis says so). Note its own ctx=32768 full row was 0.987x (21536 vs SGLang 21246 us) while every other row was >=1.000x; a 'faster' reading there must be judged against SGLang's absolute row, not against the parity's noisy one, or regression to the mean looks like a mechanism.

in flight, not landed: moe-align-side-stream moves MoE align work after attention onto a side stream; no shared launch, traffic or numerical path with the FA3 call, but if it lands first the base rows shift by a few us and the reading must use the merged base's profile.
interference: No ab-revert: the only landed hypothesis is the parity port itself, which is the base, and reverting it means the plain PyTorch kernel, not a meaningful A/B. No ab-tune: nothing landed has a knob that touches attention. No control: the two sub-changes (pay the gather; call FA3 on a contiguous buffer) are separated by the profile for free, because the index kernels and the flash::enable_sm90_or_later kernel appear as separate rows with their own us, and the parity profile already holds the paged FA3 time per shape (419.9 / 1656.1 / 907 / 4545.7 / 8164.1 us). Every outcome reads unambiguously from one run: FA3 row drops by more than the gather rows add = mechanism (i) confirmed, keep and then cheapen the gather; FA3 row unchanged = ceiling (ii), the paged gather is not the prefill limiter and the idea is closed (and it also tells fa3-batched-mode and any custom-kernel idea where the ceiling is); FA3 row drops but the gather rows eat it = re-mint with a wider-lane or Triton gather. The ambiguity the rubric asks about (both a gain and a loss uninterpretable) does not arise, so spending a second run on a companion is wasteful.
rules_flags: No rule break found: the gather runs inside kernel_fn every call on this call's cache rows (after store_cache, so the new tokens' FP8 rows are included), nothing is cached across calls, K/V bytes are copied not re-quantized (FP8 cache rule holds), q stays the same FP8 cast, every key the reference attends is in the buffer (full: the whole page table; sliding: positions seq_lens-2047 .. seq_lens+L-1, which cover the first query's left edge and the last query's right edge), and the causal/window masks over the trimmed buffer map exactly (key j at absolute start+j; allowed iff j <= i + cache_seqlens_w - L and j >= that - (window-1), the same set as over the full cache). Padding rows (page -1 -> row 0) lie beyond cache_seqlens(_w) and are masked, never attended as keys of their own.

Graph safety: all index math is fixed-shape (clamp/gather/arange on ints), no .item()/.cpu(); the per-call k_buf/v_buf (up to 2 x 83 MB at turn_4) and arange(W) are shape-sized allocations inside capture, which the rule permits (no allocating on input VALUES). Branching on config page_size for the fallback is a config branch, allowed.

scheduler_metadata is dropped; on this problem it is None for every case (reference.py:_fa3_scheduler_metadata returns None unless q_len == 1), so nothing is lost and no prepare launch moves into the timed call beyond what the parity already pays.

Precision caveat, not a break: FA3's non-paged TMA path may pick a different kBlockN / split count than the paged path, so the fp32 online-softmax accumulation order changes; the outputs stay within the 2.5x-reference bound as any FA3 config does, but do not read a tiny error drift as a bug.
open_questions: Implementation detail that decides whether the gather is 10 us or 200 us: torch advanced indexing on a float8_e4m3fn tensor may not be dispatched at all (older index kernels lack FLOAT8 types) and if it is, it moves one byte per thread. View the pool as k_cache.view(-1, hkv*d).view(torch.int64) ([rows, 16] int64, 8-byte lanes; or torch.int32 [rows, 32]) before index_select, exactly as the parity already does with .view(torch.uint8) for store_cache, then view the result back to FP8 [B, S, 2, 64]. Same bytes, same rule standing, several times cheaper. If the first run shows the index rows above ~100 us at turn_4, that is the re-mint, not a new idea.

API check that fails fast on test 1 if wrong: sgl_kernel's flash_attn_with_kvcache with page_table=None, cu_seqlens_q set and cu_seqlens_k_new None is FA3's is_varlen_q && !is_varlen_k mode, which requires k_cache.size(0) == batch (B, max_pages, 2, 64) and uses cache_seqlens as seqused_k; the sliding buffer's S = W = 2047 + L and cache_seqlens_w <= W must satisfy that. If the wrapper insists on page_table for FP8 the run dies on the first test at no scoring cost, as the hypothesis already says.

Is 600 TFLOP/s FA3's hdim-64 FP8 ceiling with contiguous KV? The judge's page-size-64 test does not answer it (64 is not a multiple of kBlockN for this config, so it is also the non-TMA path). This run is the cheapest way to find out and the answer is worth recording in FINDINGS either way, including for fa3-batched-mode (if the ceiling is intrinsic, no launch-mode change can move the first-turn rows either).

The sliding first-turn gather is 2 x 18431 x 128 B = 4.7 MB per direction, not < 3 MB as the md says; immaterial against 17 ms, but the row should still read flat and a visible loss there would point at the index-kernel cost rather than attention.

If this lands, fa3-batched-mode stacked on it becomes pure non-varlen FA3 (static scheduler, static num_splits heuristic) rather than varlen-with-dynamic-split; that is a different regime from the one the batched-mode md argues, so re-review it against the merged base rather than running it as written.
